practices.dataType: Precise location (GPS), while a navigation session the user started is running
practices.purpose: Native navigation components use the latest fix to advance route progress, time instructions and detect departure from a captured route on the device. App.tsx does not currently compose these components into installed navigation.

retention.note: The native session stores the route and latest accepted fix in SQLite, with a maximum session age of 24 hours. Termination removes location-bearing session rows; expiry is handled when navigation or recovery runs, not by a guaranteed deletion timer. Verify backup exclusion in the candidate binary.

practices.userControl: Once native navigation is composed, end the session or revoke location permission. Foreground-only mode is implemented in components and still needs installed-device qualification.

appleLabel.exemptionReason: Proposed local-processing classification for native route progress only. Rerouting and other transmitted location uses require separate review.

practices.notes: DRAFT registry: classification values are proposals pending privacy review against the exact binary, served web/API builds, deployment and providers. Native component behavior is not proof of installed availability. App.tsx does not compose navigation or system-auth dispatch.

practices.dataType: Precise location while the screen is locked or the app is in the background
practices.purpose: Native components are intended to continue guidance during a user-started session while the screen is locked or the app is backgrounded. App.tsx does not currently compose native navigation, so this behavior is unavailable in the installed shell.

retention.note: The intended native session uses the same 24-hour maximum age as foreground navigation. Termination removes its location-bearing rows; expiry cleanup requires navigation or recovery execution.

practices.userControl: The permission controller supports foreground-only mode and the coordinator supports ending navigation. Both require foreground composition and qualification in the candidate binary.

appleLabel.exemptionReason: Proposed classification for fixes processed locally by native guidance components. Installed background guidance and its data flows remain unqualified.

practices.recipient: The OpenMapX API operated by this deployment
practices.purpose: Computing directions from the start, destination and waypoints supplied to the OpenMapX API and its configured routing providers.

retention.note: Ephemeral handling is proposed. Verify API, router, cache, application/proxy logging and processor retention for the selected deployment; this registry does not establish immediate disposal.

practices.userControl: Request directions only when willing to send route inputs to this deployment and its configured providers.

practices.dataType: Current position submitted for a reroute or replan
practices.recipient: The OpenMapX API operated by this deployment
practices.purpose: Native components request a replacement route when a session leaves its route or misses a transit connection. Requests follow reroute decisions, not a continuous location stream. Installed native navigation is not currently composed.

retention.note: Ephemeral handling is proposed, as for initial route requests. Review routing/transit provider retention, request metadata, caches and deployment logs.

practices.userControl: The offline navigation components suppress network rerouting. Installed navigation and this control still require composition and device qualification.
practices.notes: Verify retry and reroute behavior in the candidate runtime. This row describes request-based rerouting, not proof that each decision produces exactly one network transmission.

practices.dataType: Transit origin, destination, departure time, and a rotating refresh token
practices.recipient: The OpenMapX API, which queries the configured schedule service
practices.purpose: Planning a journey through the API and configured transit providers. Native components also support live refresh during navigation, which is not currently composed in App.tsx. The refresh token represents itinerary state; it does not establish anonymity.

retention.note: Ephemeral classification is pending review. Native transit session payloads contain the refresh token and itinerary and are serialized to SQLite; snapshot builders strip token fields. Check API/provider state, token lifetime and cleanup separately.

practices.userControl: Avoid transit planning to avoid its request. Native components suppress live refresh offline; this is not a qualified installed-shell feature.

practices.dataType: The board-to-alight stop list of each ridden leg
practices.purpose: Native transit components use a captured board-to-alight stop list for stop counting without further network access. The list is obtained online before navigation. Installed transit navigation is not currently composed.

retention.note: Captured stops belong to the native session, whose maximum age is 24 hours. Termination deletes location-bearing session rows; expiry cleanup runs through navigation or recovery.

practices.userControl: Once native transit navigation is composed, end navigation to remove the session and its captures. Verify the complete flow on the candidate device.

practices.dataType: Scheduled local notifications for the get-off alert
practices.purpose: Native transit components can schedule an operating-system notification before the alighting stop, without a remote push service. App.tsx does not currently compose the navigation and notification ports.

retention.note: Components reconcile or cancel alerts when legs or sessions end. The proposed 24-hour budget requires verification of OS delivery and cancellation in the candidate runtime.

practices.userControl: The intended controls are disabling the alight alert or revoking notification permission. Their installed availability and behavior require qualification.

practices.dataType: Email address, display name, and authentication credentials
practices.recipient: The OpenMapX API operated by this deployment
practices.purpose: Creating and using an account for synchronized saved content and account features. Authentication uses server sessions and WebView cookies. The native system-browser helper returns handoff material rather than a session cookie; it is not currently composed into App.tsx.

retention.note: Account erasure handles live data and reports retained or failed work. Preservation rules, security/statutory retention, processors and backups need separate review; account deletion does not immediately erase every copy.

practices.userControl: Use the app without an account, or delete the account in Account Settings or at /delete-account.

practices.dataType: Saved places, labels, and app preferences
practices.recipient: The OpenMapX API operated by this deployment
practices.purpose: Synchronizing saved lists and labels across devices. The API and operators with application or database access can read them. Users can publish live or snapshot share links that anyone holding the link can read. Some app preferences remain local.

retention.note: Account deletion handles live saved data and owned share links, subject to erasure and preservation rules. Backups and copies made by share recipients are separate; revocation cannot retract recipient copies.

practices.userControl: Delete saved content or the account, and manage share links separately. Review shared content before publishing; revoke links to prevent further reads through those links.

practices.recipient: The OpenMapX API, which stores ciphertext in encrypted modes or a readable private key in explicit unencrypted mode
practices.purpose: Synchronizing the signing key used for public Mangrove reviews. Encrypted modes wrap it with a passphrase or passkey before upload. Explicit unencrypted mode stores a private JWK the server can read and use; confidentiality depends on the selected mode.

retention.note: Deleting the review identity or account removes live key records, subject to applicable erasure/preservation handling. Backup retention and exported private-key copies require separate review.

practices.userControl: Do not create a review identity; delete it, or delete the account.

practices.dataType: Review text, rating, nickname, photos and public signing identity the user chooses to publish
practices.recipient: The OpenMapX API relay and Mangrove.reviews, an independent public review commons
practices.purpose: Publishing browser-signed reviews through an authenticated OpenMapX API relay. The public signing key connects reviews under that identity. The API can associate the submission request with the signed-in account; the proposed identity classification needs review.

retention.note: OpenMapX account deletion does not retract a published public review. Key holders can submit signed edits or deletions to Mangrove. Provider retention, OpenMapX read caches and copies held by other readers require review.

practices.userControl: Choose whether to publish. Keep the signing key to edit or delete reviews later; deleting the OpenMapX account alone does not remove them.

practices.purpose: Native diagnostic components record bounded, allowlisted scalar fields locally and support deliberate export through a share sheet. There is no automatic upload path in these components. Export availability and the exact binary dependency inventory require verification.

retention.note: The repository trims diagnostics by row count and bytes and exposes explicit clearing. A 24-hour age purge is not implemented here; the retained numeric budget is a proposal pending review.

practices.userControl: The export component requires an explicit sharing action. Verify that the candidate exposes the intended export/clear controls and review any recipient handling separately.

practices.dataType: A single-use callback code and a per-attempt PKCE verifier
practices.recipient: The OpenMapX API operated by this deployment
practices.purpose: The system-browser helper returns a callback code, state and PKCE verifier through auth.result to the WebView, which sends them to the API /mobile-auth/exchange endpoint. The server checks the verifier against its stored challenge and releases a one-time token. App.tsx does not currently compose this flow.

retention.note: Codes are redeemable for two minutes and single use. The server row contains the code hash, account userId, state, challenge and encrypted token. Successful exchange deletes it; invalid attempts can leave consumed rows, and expired-row cleanup is opportunistic and subject to preservation rules. The verifier is received but not stored by this service.

practices.userControl: Cancel the browser attempt to stop completing sign-in. A row already issued by the server can remain until cleanup even if the user cancels.

appleLabel.exemptionReason: UNRESOLVED proposal, not an approved exemption. The verifier is transmitted to the API and the server row is account-linked. An opaque code and short redemption lifetime do not establish Apple real-time-only retention or Google ephemeral handling.

practices.dataType: Cookies, local storage, IndexedDB, service-worker caches and offline archives used by the web app
practices.purpose: Retaining browser state and local copies for the web UI at the compiled origin. This row describes local storage: session cookies are also sent with authenticated requests, and cached/offline data comes from network-backed features covered separately.

retention.note: Sign-out invalidates the account session and clears the active review key and its query envelope; saved-data mirroring also handles observed sign-out. It does not clear all local storage, caches or downloaded offline areas. Each store has its own expiry, eviction or explicit removal behavior.

practices.userControl: Sign out to end the account session. Remove offline areas and clear recent map data through their separate controls; clearing app/site data depends on the platform and must be verified.

practices.dataType: Tile and imagery requests revealing the viewed area, with network metadata such as IP address
practices.recipient: The map tile and imagery providers this deployment is configured to use
practices.purpose: Loading map tiles and imagery from the configured sources. Request coordinates or tile paths reveal the viewed area; direct provider requests also expose network metadata to that provider.

retention.note: Provider retention is not established by this registry. The retained ephemeral values are proposals pending review of each selected provider, intermediary, cache and log configuration.

practices.userControl: Operators select hosted or self-hosted sources. Users should review the deployment disclosures; local map downloads do not cover every imagery or media source.

practices.dataType: Install, crash and delivery data collected by Apple and Google
practices.recipient: Apple and Google, as the app's distributors
practices.purpose: Store distribution, updates and optional platform diagnostics are governed by Apple/Google settings and terms. Review the candidate binary and developer-console access before deciding what the distributor collects or makes available to the operator.

retention.note: Review the applicable store retention terms and user diagnostics settings. The retained account-lifetime value is a proposal and does not establish a store retention period.

practices.userControl: The operating system's own diagnostics and analytics settings.
practices.notes: Pending review of distributor handling, developer access and the exact binary SDK inventory. The retained not-collected values do not establish a real-time-processing exemption or prove that the operator receives no store diagnostics.
